title: AWS Introduces Preview of Well-Architected Agent
gist: AWS previewed a Well-Architected Agent that analyzes environments across 65+ services, prioritizes recommendations by business goals and reviews Terraform and CloudFormation. Practitioners question where business goals come from and the risk of automated fixes, while Corey Quinn asks what AWS Partners will do.

insights.claim: The AWS Well-Architected Agent analyzes environments against Well-Architected best practices and prioritizes recommendations across cost, security, performance and reliability, with remediation steps and pre-deployment review of Terraform and CloudFormation.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: AWS is embedding architectural review into an AI agent and shift-left IaC workflows.
insights.quote: the preview of the Well-Architected Agent, a service that analyzes environments against Well-Architected best practices

insights.claim: It correlates utilization metrics, resource configurations and application topology across 65+ AWS services and aligns recommendations to declared business goals, with implementation packages and cross-pillar trade-offs.
insights.speaker: Channy Yun
insights.so_what: Context-aware prioritization is the differentiator from the older rule-based Well-Architected Tool.
insights.quote: delivers implementation packages with every finding, and surfaces cross-pillar trade-offs
insights.locator: Channy Yun, lead blogger at AWS

insights.claim: The agent is available only in three US regions, though workloads from any region can be onboarded, and only to customers with Business Support+ or higher.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Gating by support tier turns the agent into an upsell lever for premium support plans.
insights.quote: available only in three US regions

insights.claim: AWS warns the AI-generated recommendations may contain errors or be incomplete and should be evaluated with oversight and safeguards.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Human review remains required, limiting autonomous remediation for now.
insights.locator: While the agent represents an evolution

insights.claim: Prioritizing by business goals is hard because most enterprises never documented whether a workload should trade cost for resilience, which is exactly the call a recommendation must make.
insights.speaker: Nicolas Payette
insights.so_what: The agent's value is bounded by the quality of declared business context.
insights.quote: in most enterprises nobody ever wrote down whether a given workload should trade cost for resilience

insights.claim: The risky step is moving from recommendations to automation-ready fixes, since saving money can hurt resilience and improving performance can increase cost.
insights.speaker: Alex Kargin
insights.so_what: Automated cross-pillar remediation needs guardrails against unintended trade-offs.
insights.quote: Saving money can hurt resilience, and improving performance can increase cost.

insights.claim: Corey Quinn suggests the agent offers architect-level review to accounts that cannot get a solutions architect on the phone and asks what 5,000 undifferentiated AWS Partners are left to do if it works.
insights.speaker: Corey Quinn
insights.so_what: AI agents threaten the consulting and partner ecosystem built around AWS architectural reviews.
insights.quote: what are 5,000 undifferentiated AWS "Partners" left to do?

insights.claim: Programmatic access is available through APIs and the AWS MCP Server so recommendations can be integrated into existing development and operations workflows.
insights.speaker: Channy Yun
insights.so_what: MCP integration positions AWS advice as an input to coding agents.
insights.quote: try the AWS MCP Server and plugins with your preferred AI coding tool
